Both ready, each seeded with a deliberately misspelled tag — **`referance`** on the Wikipedia link — so you can feel what fixing it is like. Please try repairing that typo and adding a new tag in each.

**Version A — one "edit" form** — http://maker:4001/edittags-a.html
Click the **pencil (✎)** on the Wikipedia link. It opens a small form with the **title and all tags together** in editable fields. Fix `referance` → `reference` in the tags box (existing tags are suggested as you type), maybe add another tag, then Save.

**Version B — edit the tags right where they sit** — http://maker:4001/edittags-b.html
Each tag chip now has a little **×**. Click the × on **`referance`** to remove it, then click **"＋ tag"** and type `reference` (suggestions appear) to add the correct one. Tags change immediately, one at a time.

The underlying difference: **A** is "open the whole thing, edit everything, save" — deliberate and all-in-one. **B** is "poke at individual tags in place" — faster for a one-tag tweak, no explicit save step.

Which feels more like how you'd want to fix and add tags? And with the one you prefer — does anything about it feel off (for example, in B tags change instantly with no undo; in A you have to open the form even for a tiny change)?
